description: Table 3 is a two-column, seven-row (one header + six data rows) reference table rendered as an image, titled "VUMAT state-dependent variable definition and allocation". The left column header is "Variable name" and the right column header is "VUMAT allocation". The left column lists six physical quantities with their mathematical symbols, and the right column assigns each to one state-dependent variable slot in the ABAQUS VUMAT user subroutine: Equivalent plastic strain (ε_p^n) → SDV1; Equivalent plastic strain rate (ε̇_p^n) → SDV2; Dislocation density (ρ_f) → SDV3; Flow stress (σ_flow) → SDV4; Yield strength (σ_y) → SDV5; Grain size (d_f) → SDV6. The table contains no numerical data, no units and no measured values — it is a purely definitional mapping between the model's internal state variables and their storage indices. Its role in the paper is to document how the modified Johnson–Cook constitutive equation (Eq. 6) is encoded in the VUMAT subroutine for Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel, so that dislocation density (ρ_f) and grain size (d_f) — the two microstructural variables added to the model to capture dislocation strengthening and grain refinement during warm multiaxial forging (MAF) — are tracked as SDV3 and SDV6 at every integration point, alongside the classic J-C variables strain, strain rate, flow stress and yield strength.

observations.observation: The table has two columns with the exact headers 'Variable name' and 'VUMAT allocation', and six data rows.
Equivalent plastic strain (ε_p^n) is allocated to SDV1.
Equivalent plastic strain rate (ε̇_p^n) is allocated to SDV2.
Dislocation density (ρ_f) is allocated to SDV3.
Flow stress (σ_flow) is allocated to SDV4.
Yield strength (σ_y) is allocated to SDV5.
Grain size (d_f) is allocated to SDV6.
The table prints no numerical values, units or tolerances; it is purely a name-to-SDV-index mapping.
The caption states the table defines and allocates VUMAT state-dependent variables.
The citing text states that the implemented user subroutine uses six state-dependent variables (SDVs), as shown in Table 3.
The citing text states that the VUMAT subroutine in ABAQUS was constructed for Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C steel to implement the modified J-C constitutive equation (Eq. 6).
The citing text states that MAF-1, MAF-3 and MAF-5 experimental results were used for comparison with the finite element simulation.
The citing text refers to Fig. 11 as the flow chart of the developed VUMAT subroutine, a separate figure from this table.
